about_the_game:
2012.

Smartphones were still new.

On a quiet night, you take out your phone and send a message, as you always do.

"I'm on my way."

It should have been just an ordinary message — or so it seemed.

---

"I'm On My Way" is a first-person horror adventure that unfolds through a smartphone chat interface.

As you walk through the night city, you communicate with "Sugimoto" through your phone, making your way toward his apartment.

But something about the conversation feels off.

A path you don’t remember.
Events you’ve never experienced.
And things that should not exist.

The rumors Sugimoto tells begin to overwrite reality itself.

---

A night where you can only keep moving forward.

What will you say?
Will you trust his words?

Your words will shape the outcome.

---

■ Unease behind the screen

All interactions take place through your phone

■ A city that distorts

With every conversation, something begins to change

■ Words that decide your fate

What you type influences events and endings

---

Is that message truly just a simple notification?

content_descriptors.notes:
This game contains intense horror sequences and unsettling imagery.
It may not be suitable for players who are disturbed by horror or grotesque content.

mac_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: macOS 13 Ventura or later (Intel or Apple Silicon)
  • Processor: Apple M1 / Intel Core i5-8259U
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Apple M1 GPU / Intel Iris Plus 655
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Built-in macOS compatible sound device
mac_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: macOS 13 Ventura or later (Intel or Apple Silicon)
  • Processor: Apple M1 Pro or better / Intel Core i7-9750H or better
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Apple M1 Pro GPU or better / AMD Radeon Pro 5500M or better
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Built-in macOS compatible sound device

short_description: On a quiet night, you text your friend Sugimoto: “I’m on my way.” This first-person horror adventure unfolds through smartphone chats. Walk the city at night, face strange encounters, and make choices that lead you to his room. Can you trust the words on your screen?
